I have very conflicting thoughts about Sandrock. 

I really like the progression and resource gathering loop - it never feels unrewarding and there's not too much of a grind to get the resources you need to make something. Going into the mines usually nets you with a lot of resources and ore you need to progress, and the progression never feels slow. It's paced quite well. I do appreciate that the furnaces and crafting stations run on in-game time, so if something is taking forever to smelt - you can just go sleep until the next day and it's done. That is quite a nice feature.

The combat kinda sucks - it's shallow and unsatisfying. It kind of feels like those freemium anime RPGs that are meant to be played for an hour before shilling out like ten bucks. The combat might be the most disappointing thing to me. The skill trees are also quite shallow.

Where the game really falters is the actual town and villagers. Wow - I hate literally all the characters. They are annoying and have terrible writing. For a life-sim, the characters usually need to be a little charming or well written, but after like ten hours of gameplay I just found myself skipping all the cutscenes and dialogue. It's upsetting because you can tell that a lot of the game is meant to center around the characters. In the time you're out of stamina and waiting for things to craft, you're supposed to interact with the characters and complete relationship quests, but the characters all suck! A lot of them talk and act like children, which is kinda odd to me. The character designs are also weird looking, but that's just the art style, which does give the game a unique look to it.

I also ran into some performance issues on the Steam Deck, which was a little disappointing because I like playing life/farming sims on a handheld.

If you're looking to buy Sandrock as a life-sim, I wouldn't buy it. There are other games that do character writing and story far better, but if you just want a game to grind out resources and progress your workshop - this game does that pretty well. I'll probably keep playing, but I'm still going to ignore anything that has to do with character interactions.

Originally played My Time at Portia and absolutely loved it even though it was buggy and unfinished. Ended up encountering a game-breaking bug after tons of progress so I kept my eye on the development of this game. Sandrock is the least interesting of the inworld cities to me but the claims that the game was completed unlike Portia drew me in and I eventually caved and got it on sale. Needless to say, I've tried to play 3 times now and hit a bug a few minutes in each time that freezes the whole game. Plus it isn't finished--not just because of the bugs, but there's incomplete voice acting. So it's the same issue as with My Time at Portia. I unfortunately won't be following this series anymore because it has so much promise but the devs seem short or time or willingness to clean up bugs. I now own two unplayable games.

Unrelated to the games being unplayable, I've been disappointed with how the character creation doesn't let you make a character remotely similar to the in-game characters and unless you're going for a certain aesthetic your character feels clunky/wonky compared to the others.

I’ve put 180+ hours into My Time at Sandrock and really loved it.
The world and characters are great but the longer you play, the worse the performance gets.

After a while, the UI becomes painfully slow. Changing areas makes icons and interaction prompts take forever to load. The game doesn’t crash, it just slowly grinds your patience down. My PC can handle this game easily, and changing settings doesn’t fix it.
I reported the issue a long time ago to the devs and got nowhere. It’s incredibly frustrating to invest this much time into a game only for it to bog down like this.

No new updates have come out either and most likely never will as the team is now fully focused on My Time at Evershine. I do think this issue will never get fixed.
As much as I enjoyed Sandrock, I can’t recommend it knowing it eventually becomes this tedious to play.

!!! DISCLAIMER: FOR ALL PEOPLE ONLY BUYING FOR MULTIPLAYER: IT IS A SCAM !!! 
The singleplayer is fine I guess, but the tag multiplayer should be removed and it is a scam because it is a bare-bones version of the game (missing mechanics, story, the map is different, the skills, the balancing ... it is a completely diffferent game and feels like they used their alpha for the multiplayer). 
The developers do not communicate this at all on their steam page, It is never mentioned that you don't get to play the real game if you want to play multiplayer only and they should be ashamed of themselves for that. If you are only interested in singleplayer you can disregard this.

If you are buying this for the "multiplayer experience" advertised on the box, don't. It is not a co-op version of the game; it is a hollowed-out, broken shell.

The Facts:
Zero Story: The rich, character-driven plot of the single-player campaign is completely absent. Multiplayer is a mindless "sandbox" where you just grind milestones with no narrative context.

No Progress Transfer: You cannot use your single-player character. Progress is tied to the specific server/world. If you play on a friend's world, you gain nothing for your own.

Gutted Mechanics: Key features like the Factory and Greenhouse are missing in co-op. It feels like playing an early alpha version of the actual game.

Shared Wallet & Resources: Money is shared globally. One "creative" friend can spend the entire group's savings on furniture, leaving everyone else unable to buy basic mission supplies.

Technical Mess: Constant desync, disappearing items, and 5–10 minute loading screens between areas. Quest triggers frequently break, forcing all players to restart the day.

Server Limits: You are locked to one character per region. Want to play with a different group of friends? You often have to delete your existing character and all their progress.

Verdict:
A total failure in cooperative design. It’s a repetitive building simulator that strips away everything that makes Sandrock good.

After 199 hours in the game. I can not recommend it.  I discovered today that I was actually playing two games. One is the open sandbox crafting game with RPG elements advertised to the customer on Steams store page falsely by Panthea, and then the actual game which is a linear visual novel that cares nothing about the player, or what the player does in the game because all events are pre determined by the the games writer.  Turns out none of your choices actual matter in the game, and nothing kills a games immersion faster than developers making the Main Story the actual Main Character of the game. 

I uninstalled the game today after doing the Main Story quest where the games evil empire attacks Sandrock. The developers build this event up through multiple quest, and by the time the event triggers my character had maxed out every stat, max gear, could build anything in the game instantly because having hundreds of every resource, an industrial set up that had me close to a million in game currency, and strong enough she could one shot pretty much every enemy in the game. Turns out none of that matters. Your character could punch a hole through reality itself, but the Main Story is the Main Character. Not You. 
This is where the games mask comes off, and reveals the actual game to the player.  A cinematic visual novel cosplaying as a crafting RPG game where nothing the player actual does matters. You get forced into defeat because the Main Story demands it, then forced into another submissive situation that your character has no choice but to comply with even though you already defeated everyone. Reinforcing that you, and nothing you do in the game makes a difference.  It was quite disappointing, and for me the game ended when I won that fight. Because I refuse to be subjected to such blatant disrespect by the developers for the time I invested into the game, and into the character. Losing is perfectly acceptable in a game when the players own planning, and skills are not enough, or when the unwinnable fight is just the precursor to the actual fight. Dark Souls does this fantastically, and not because a linear story pretending to have RPG elements demands it.   

I was honestly looking forward to "My Time in Evershine" up until today, but not anymore. Maybe, and that's big maybe if Panthea makes the player the main character in "My Time in Evershine", and not the person they hired to write the story. I might entertain purchasing it. But as of right now, I wouldn't recommend any games by this developer if you are a fan of the crafting/RPG/Sandbox games because as of right now the way they design their games, your character is nothing more than a NPC's to the main story. Not someone who actually plays a part in how the story really turns out.

Basically, something irked me so many times, that I eventually decided to come make a review, out of irritation. When I beat a game, and I don't have that feeling, it gets a good review usually. I wanted to enjoy this game, I REALLY wanted to. I was drawn in by the idea that romantic candidates could come to you themselves, and how the relationships in general were very organic and real. But unfortunately I didn't have a chance to get that far before I started to dislike the game.

I understand that this game has a specific style, but I just didn't enjoy the player customization. It was very limited in terms of body types. You can be small or smaller. When I got to actually playing it felt like I was a 12 year old with how gangly my character was, despite being a literal builder. The bartender is more jacked than me.

I did enjoy the voice acting, but it just doesn't fit with how lacking the characters are in expressions. Rocky especially looks like a neglected hamster. It makes it hard to take anything seriously.

These are personal problems and you can still enjoy the game on your own, but if these things are important to you then I wouldn't play.

I have 113 hours into this game and I played and finished My Time at Portia.  Upon beating the main story I got the Steam achievement “Jewel of the Eufaula – Complete the main story.”… 8.2% of players have that achievement.  I really wanted to like this game, but there are way more bad things than good, so it is uneven and just not a good game in my opinion.

So how come only 8.2% of the people playing finsihed the main story?!?!?  Well, the games story plays out of order.  You WILL feel like you have finished the main story about 80 hours in.  The story line will FEEL like the end, but its not.  Everything after that main story end feeling is boring and very repetitive. 

Its like they just threw in some extra crap to keep you busy for no real reason.  They introduce new people you can have relationships with, be friends with and might make you mad you are married to who you have,  they give you armor and weapons you are not high enough level to use, and have ruins that are level 80-90, but no quests or reason to do them… When I bet the game I JUST hit 50, to get to 80 is crazy.

Also the pacing of this game is off.  You don’t need to unlock most of the shop land and only need the best workstation (I NEVER used the factory, it was not needed or required to use).  The UI is pretty bad after you use it for a while. ALWAYS having the “new” icon on everything is super annoying and you can’t clear them very easy at all.  The skill tree is super pointless and you end up getting most of the useful stuff very quick then the rest of the game you are just filling blank spot that don’t mean anything.  Why do I want to put points in sword and shield when I use dagger weapons??

There are lots of things that make the game more annoying vs helping.  At one point I had to make some bush sculptures, but I needed a certain kind of plant… which I didn’t have and I could only get from growing it.  Growing TAKES FOREVER, so I was locked into playing hours to let the plants grow OR sleep over and over to make time fly.  You also cannot do anything to speed time up.  If I run out of things to do at 3pm, but I need to meet someone at 10pm, I have to find something to do for that time.

Portia is a MUCH better game outside of the graphic and size of the land (which has its own issues… there is TONS of space, but you don’t and won’t use/see most of it).

I’ll still give My time at Evershine a chance since they could fix most of the bad things in this game.

It's fine, but I remember enjoying Portia more. This game's main quest progresses way too slowly. Since the main quest unlocks things, it just feels like a hard lock. There are typically multiple in game days between steps in the main quest and this is where all the time is wasted. Sometimes you could simply skip days, other times you have a "meet in the evening at this place" to progress the quest. Maybe you don't actually have to, I haven't risked it...but this means I have to either speed up the game timer or find some way to use the whole day.

This wasn't a problem early game, but I'd say it's been a slog since about hour 30. Looking at the list of main quests, it doesn't look like I'm even halfway through.

I don't want to be rushed. I like the cozy aspect. I think it would be a lot better if the next quest just triggered immediately instead of days later. I don't think it would ruin any sense of "realism"...there's plenty of "hurry up!" dialogue that makes you think an actual world is progressing without you; it's not, it will wait for you. Knowing this, I don't see any harm in removing arbitrary delays.

Plenty of other things have improved since Portia but the pacing makes me prefer the first game. Worth playing if you don't mind a very slow experience past the early stages. But I wouldn't say I recommend it.

Edit: And it's so buggy...nothing gamebreaking, just constant annoyances. I don't remember the last game I played that was this buggy.

The lore, story, world bulding, voice acting and art design are very good.

But anything gameplay-related is ass. I don't even understand it myself. Portia was great vom beginning to finish. But this one is ... painfully slow. They are really similar and as its successor it should be better, right? But it isn't. In Portia, every day seemed like an opportunity and your schedule was tight. Here, it is slow. The pacing is really bad. And the loading times and animation whenever you start a conversation, open the inventory, go through a door etc. are such a time waster.

The text below was originally from my refund request but since it never got granted I might as well share it here.

"I thought long and hard about buying this game because I wasn't a fan of the desert setting, but I had heard so many people talk about how it was a better game than My Time at Portia and so much more fun that I finally bit the bullet and decided to give it a try. Massive time sink required to get anywhere in this game.  Nearly everything you do, be it a quests or refining items, are on a timer.  Refining materials takes a very long time and once refined, you're not guarantee you'll get the items you need to craft item and complete a quest.  I deplore game design like this.

Your mailbox quickly fills up with time sensitive letters.  Couple that with trying to get the first quest done, and the game easily becomes overwhelming.  If I could refund this game, I would but I've missed the return window.

You know, if they removed the timers, this would be an amazing game.  But as it sits, it's nothing but hurry up and wait.

It has a few good systems but ultimately they arent properly implemented or polished and the more you play the more the game reveals all its weaknesses.  The story is frankly corny and pretty terrible and the gameplays focus is to consume your time rather than to be engaging and fun. Severe lack of polish and bugs make this feel like a game that just got released to early access. Further, it's really just not that fun for a life sim. Mining and combat are dull and dangerous ruins are truly awful and shouldn't be in the game. It's also kind of frustrating that it's really hard to find gifts that people actually like without a guide since there are so many items. I will say there are a lot of cutscenes and events with the townspeople if you care about that.

I loved this games predecessor "My Time At Portia" and everything I loved about that game was destroyed in this game. 

My first rule of any game is that if something detracts from the enjoyment of the game, even if it is a reasonable mechanic, it should not be part of the game. For example, when I run a D&D game, all my players have an infinite bag of holding, so they don't have to worry about weight encumbrance. Enter this game... set in the desert, so you have to constantly clear sand off of everything. You also have to gather water over and over to keep things running, and you are not allowed to cut down trees, even though you need wood. This game has a lot of things like that. Things that are there to sap enjoyment from the game, not enhance it. 

My Time at Portia had amazing characters. I can't stand the characters in this game. I got it in early access, because I love the Portia game so much, and I remember reading the back story of one of the potential romantic partners. The back story they were gushing about was that this girl abandoned her husband and kids. If you ever had that happen to you, I am betting you hate this girl. Everyone is just unlikable in my opinion. 

Like it's predecessor, this game has a calendar with special events, but quests also have set timers, and you will frequently be forced to skip the fun event because your quest requires you to be somewhere else entirely. 

The new system for resources and what amounts to dungeons is vastly inferior to the previous game. To the point they are not really enjoyable. 

A big part of your game is recycling crap into usable materials, but you can't recycle fast enough to make progress quickly. Partly that is because you can't gather the stuff to put into a recycler fast enough, and with a couple different types of things to recycle you need more than one recycle machine, but you won't have the water to keep them all running. 

The new interface for crafting is confusing, and has a learning curve. It is much harder to use. In the previous game, I would plan ahead for crafting things by having certain chests contain the materials I needed for something that was coming up. The I would put the items I needed into my inventory before I started crafting. That way if I was crafting something else that used the same materials, I was keeping the items I needed in the future safe from use. This is gone now, as it will take everything from your inventory, and you can't really organize to plan ahead. The interface is also visually unappealing. 

I give the previous game a 15/10 and this on a 1/10. Avoid it if you can.

You walk around town admiring all the NPC's homes having little stoves and kitchen sinks, counter tops for 23 hours...

and then you make your first cooking station and you can't put it inside your shipping container. 

You have to cook outside.

I thought this was a cozy game like harvest moon or something. You cant have a cozy game without a home to be cozy in.

I wish I could give a score for a review instead of an or off option. I wouldn't buy it again knowing you don't have a home to pimp out, but the premise/story/aesthetic of the game was good (combat was kind of gross and the character turns from outside of the center of its rotation which is weird also). I think the deciding factor for giving a down-vote for other people is that the aesthetic draws you into thinking its a cozy game but its like a factory making game or something, I wont get far enough to find out.

"What if, in a game where you need tons of resources to make anything, we just don't give you resources?"

It gives me no pleasure to give my first negative review on Steam to this game. I enjoyed Portia and I wanted to like this game. The setting was.... different. And some of the concepts are intriguing and fresh - salvaging over mining. But unlike all the games like this one, after several game days, I didn't feel even a little further ahead. I'd spend all day and all my energy scraping together enough wood to make one storage box which barely holds anything.

The one big plus is being able to save whenever you want. That's a feature I wish Portia had. Other than that, the gameplay, the characters, they just don't work for me.
